A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Autoencoding Random Forests by the same authors. All 25 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including Appendices A–D, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on 20 tabular datasets, MNIST experiments, genomic-data applications, and decoder and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds runtime comparisons and RFAE training and inference measurements in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The RF kernel and diffusion-map encoder, Nyström projection, constrained optimization, split relabeling, k-NN decoding, and Appendix C greedy algorithm remain unchanged. The expanded kernel derivation does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 20 tabular datasets, MNIST, mouse-brain batch-correction application, and leukemia embeddings. The new runtime studies reuse existing tabular datasets without introducing new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: TVAE, TTVAE, AE, and VAE remain the reconstruction comparators, and v2 times this same comparator set. The decoder and convolutional-autoencoder comparisons are retained. Newly discussed related autoencoders are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 adds runtime protocols: a controlled five-method comparison on three datasets using a laptop, and CPU-only RFAE training/inference measurements at compression factor 0.2. The original reconstruction splits, distortion metric, model settings, and other experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds empirical computational-cost and scalability analyses, comparing methods' runtimes and separating RFAE training and inference costs across datasets. The existing decoder comparison, MNIST parameter sweeps, and supervised-versus-unsupervised embedding analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The retained distortion table changes its uncertainty label from standard deviation to standard errors without changing values. New timing studies specify 100 runs per method and 10 runs per dataset, respectively; these are not increases to the original bootstrap counts. Runtime uncertainty reporting has unresolved issues, including marketing's total mean of 240.46 seconds and reported uncertainty of 7889.97.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 add runtime results. For credit, Table 3 reports RFAE at 1379.5 seconds, versus TVAE at 2212.5 and TTVAE at 4046.0, while AE and VAE are faster. All retained distortion scores and rankings, including RFAE's average rank of 1.80, are unchanged; moving the reconstruction table does not add results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an explicit algebraic derivation establishing equality between the scaled RF feature-map inner product and Equation 1. This extends the existing proof, while theorem statements, regularity assumptions A1–A5, and the remaining proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about principled RF autoencoding, kernel properties, decoder consistency, and applications. The added efficiency evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the runtime results as an efficiency advantage over TVAE/TTVAE but a disadvantage against AE/VAE, and adds a scalability interpretation. The discussion also removes v1's assertion that only one hyperparameter needs attention and points to the already-existing sensitivity analysis.

D1.justification: Section 5 replaces the generic supplementary-code statement with an explicit bips-hb/RFAE repository pointer. Appendix B.2 documents hardware and execution settings for the new timing experiments. Existing software packages, preprocessing instructions, and reconstruction hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive comparisons with Carreira-Perpiñán and Gazizov's tree autoencoder and Aumon et al.'s RF-informed neural autoencoder. Further citations connect RFAE to supervised dimensionality reduction and kernel approximation. These refine the existing positioning without replacing its central novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted terminology and discussion edits, expands related-work and derivation explanations, repairs the unfinished VAE sentence, and updates the conference footer. The section hierarchy and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v1's appendix reconstruction Table 2 becomes main-text Table 1, while main-text Figure 4 moves to Appendix B.2 as Figure 5. v2 adds runtime Tables 3–4 and adjusts figure placement, sizing, and captions. The existing empirical plots and image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The runtime measurements make efficiency tradeoffs more assessable, while the explicit kernel derivation, closer related-work comparisons, and concrete code pointer improve clarity and reproducibility. These are limited gains around unchanged methods and main results. Table 4 lists 19 datasets despite claiming 20 and contains unexplained extreme uncertainty values, weakening the new scalability evidence.
